sample_unit: claims (benchmark datasets HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, SciFact; counts not reported in text)

links.outcome: Hallucination mitigation and claim verification performance when LLM outputs are grounded in retrieved biomedical evidence
links.effect: Authors report CER, which grounds LLM reasoning in retrieved scientific evidence, mitigates hallucination risk and achieves state-of-the-art performance on HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, and SciFact; no numeric results in provided text.
links.quote: By integrating the text-generation capabilities of large language models with advanced retrieval techniques for high-quality biomedical scientific evidence, CER effectively mitigates the risk of hallucinations, ensuring that generated outputs are grounded in verifiable, evidence-based sources.

unlisted_practices: Supervised veracity prediction layered on top of retrieval and LLM reasoning for biomedical fact-checking

screen.reason: Evaluates a proposed multimodal/LLM framework (CER) combining retrieval and reasoning to fact-check biomedical claims against standard benchmark datasets (HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, SciFact).
